decoder_context: ℕ+ is the type of positive natural numbers. Fin m consists of natural values strictly less than m; .val extracts the value. Even is parity. Natural subtraction is truncated.

A dependent sum Σ b, C b consists of a label b and an element of its carrier C b. A finite function type indexes all assignments of one value to each argument. EuclideanSpace ℝ J is the real coordinate space indexed by J, with the Euclidean norm.
WithLp.toLp 2 regards the same finite array as a Euclidean vector; it does not alter its entries. A dependent function space has the product measurable structure.
stdGaussian is the centered identity-covariance Borel probability law on a real Euclidean space. Measure.pi is the product measure. HasLaw f μ P asserts AEMeasurable f P and Measure.map f P = μ.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.Probability.HasLaw
import Mathlib.Probability.ProductMeasure
import Mathlib.Data.PNat.Basic

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

noncomputable section

/-!
# Joint Gaussian law of the ordered coefficient blocks

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1 (CC BY 4.0), §4.1.1 after Eq. (15).
The entrywise inverse of the direct-sum collection sends the actual
unconditioned standard Gaussian to the product of the block laws.
The target dependent function type is used as a measurable product, not
as a claim that its default norm is the direct-sum norm.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.CoefficientBlocks

/-- Regroup the flat ordered coordinates without changing any coefficient.
The product law supplies the standard Gaussian marginals and mutual independence.
The isolated identity does not require the paper's large-dimension choice of
level depth and makes no claim after conditioning on admissibility. -/
theorem jointCoefficientBlocks_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) :
    let B := Fin (h + 1) × {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let blocks := fun (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)) (b : B) ↦
      (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun c : C b ↦ ξ ⟨b, c⟩) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))
    HasLaw blocks (Measure.pi fun b : B ↦ stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)))
      (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b))) := by
  intro B C blocks
  classical
  let flat : Measure ((Σ b : B, C b) → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi fun _ ↦ gaussianReal 0 1
  let grouped : Measure (∀ b : B, C b → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi fun b ↦ Measure.pi fun _ : C b ↦ gaussianReal 0 1
  let split := MeasurableEquiv.piCurry (fun (b : B) (_ : C b) ↦ ℝ)
  let wrap (x : ∀ b : B, C b → ℝ) (b : B) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b) :=
    WithLp.toLp 2 (x b)
  have hmBlocks : Measurable blocks := by
    dsimp [blocks]
    fun_prop
  have hmWrap : Measurable wrap := by
    dsimp [wrap]
    fun_prop
  have hSplit : flat.map split = grouped := by
    simpa only [flat, grouped, split, Measure.infinitePi_eq_pi] using
      Measure.infinitePi_map_piCurry (fun (b : B) (_ : C b) ↦ gaussianReal 0 1)
  have hFactor (b : B) :
      (Measure.pi (fun _ : C b ↦ gaussianReal 0 1)).map
        (WithLp.toLp 2 : (C b → ℝ) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)) =
      stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)) :=
    map_pi_eq_stdGaussian
  let : ∀ b : B, SigmaFinite ((Measure.pi (fun _ : C b ↦ gaussianReal 0 1)).map
      (WithLp.toLp 2 : (C b → ℝ) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))) := by
    intro b
    rw [hFactor b]
    infer_instance
  have hWrap : grouped.map wrap =
      Measure.pi fun b : B ↦ stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)) := by
    rw [show grouped.map wrap = Measure.pi (fun b : B ↦
      (Measure.pi (fun _ : C b ↦ gaussianReal 0 1)).map
        (WithLp.toLp 2 : (C b → ℝ) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))) from
      Measure.pi_map_pi (fun b ↦ (by fun_prop : Measurable
        (WithLp.toLp 2 : (C b → ℝ) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))).aemeasurable)]
    exact congrArg Measure.pi (funext hFactor)
  have hFlat : flat.map (WithLp.toLp 2) =
      stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)) :=
    map_pi_eq_stdGaussian
  have hCompose : blocks ∘ (WithLp.toLp 2) = wrap ∘ split := rfl
  refine ⟨hmBlocks.aemeasurable, ?_⟩
  rw [← hFlat, Measure.map_map hmBlocks (by fun_prop), hCompose,
    ← Measure.map_map hmWrap split.measurable, hSplit, hWrap]

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.CoefficientBlocks

publication_context.statement: Draw independent centered identity-covariance Gaussian tensors Ξ_i,p in the stated ordered tensor spaces. Collect them into the Euclidean direct sum. The collected vector has its centered identity-covariance Gaussian law. Equivalently, grouping the coordinates of that joint Gaussian returns the product of the block standard Gaussian laws.
assumptions: In the paper n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated finite law holds for all positive integer n and natural h; admissibility is not generalized.
The independent standard Gaussian tensor blocks range over levels i=0,…,h and even degrees p=4,6,…,P. Each block retains the ordered tensor carrier with n^(pS_i) coordinates.
The law is unconditioned. The family carrier has the product measurable structure; the Euclidean geometry is on the ℓ² direct sum, not the default dependent-function norm.

obligations.label: Preserve every ordered level/degree coefficient coordinate
Derive the measurable unconditioned joint-to-product law

lesson.title: Split the joint Gaussian into its coefficient blocks
assumptions: In the paper n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated finite law holds for all positive integer n and natural h; admissibility is not generalized.
The independent standard Gaussian tensor blocks range over levels i=0,…,h and even degrees p=4,6,…,P. Each block retains the ordered tensor carrier with n^(pS_i) coordinates.
The law is unconditioned. The family carrier has the product measurable structure; the Euclidean geometry is on the ℓ² direct sum, not the default dependent-function norm.
lesson.statement: Under the actual joint standard Gaussian, each coordinate block has its standard Gaussian law, and the entire family has their product law. This is mutual independence, not only zero covariance or pairwise independence.
lesson.reader_note: The paper goes from independent draws to a single Euclidean vector. The Lean law uses the inverse entrywise map. Neither orientation changes a coordinate or a variance.

steps.title: Identify the ordered direct-sum coordinates
steps.text: Let b=(i,p). Each tensor slot is a choice of a copy of the trailing tensor, then a trailing block and one of its repeated factors. A coordinate chooses one of n entries in each slot. Tag it by b so that grouping and flattening are inverse, with no duplicate or lost coordinate.
steps.formula: \begin{gathered}K=2^{74(h+1)},\quad P=2^{64(h+1)},\quad S_i=\sum_{j=0}^{h-i}K^j,\\ T_b=\{(r,j,k):0\le r<p,\ 0\le j\le h-i,\ 0\le k<K^j\},\\ C_b=\{c:T_b\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\},\quad E_b=\mathbb R^{C_b},\quad |C_b|=n^{pS_i},\\ \mathcal G_n=\bigoplus_{b\in B}E_b,\qquad \operatorname{group}(\xi)_b(c)=\xi_{(b,c)}.\end{gathered}
steps.lean: Fin(P+1) keeps the upper endpoint P, and the subtype retains the lower endpoint and parity. The dependent sum Σ b, C b realizes the flat coordinate index. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps each coordinate array, rather than applying a stochastic transformation.

steps.title: Group independent scalar coordinates
steps.text: On the flat Euclidean space the standard Gaussian is the scalar standard-normal product, written in Euclidean coordinates. The grouping map partitions this product into the same blocks. On measurable rectangles both sides give the product of exactly the same scalar probabilities.
steps.lean: map_pi_eq_stdGaussian realizes the flat Gaussian. MeasurableEquiv.piCurry regroups the sigma-indexed array; infinitePi_map_piCurry and infinitePi_eq_pi give the identity for these finite index types.

steps.title: Read the marginals and independence
steps.text: Wrap each scalar block into its Euclidean carrier. A coordinatewise pushforward of a product is the product of the corresponding pushforwards, so each block becomes a standard Gaussian. Product evaluation gives the marginals; the same joint identity proves mutual independence for all blocks together.
steps.lean: Measure.pi_map_pi performs the blockwise pushforward. Each map in the composition is measurable, and hCompose identifies the composition entrywise with the stated map. The focused test applies measurePreserving_eval and iIndepFun_iff_map_fun_eq_pi_map to the actual theorem.

lesson.lean_statement: HasLaw includes almost-everywhere measurability and the exact pushforward measure identity. No marginal, independence, norm equality or assumed coefficient law is a public premise.
lesson.lean_proof: Three moves: represent the flat Gaussian by scalar coordinates, regroup those coordinates, and transport every grouped product to the Euclidean block Gaussian. The only probability infrastructure is from pinned Mathlib; the paper-specific contribution is its exact ordered carrier and law.
lesson.dependency_notes: No extra ASTIS wrapper is introduced. The earlier scalar angular theorem uses the same tensor carrier but is not called by this proof. The prefix law, degree-summed field and conditional level iteration are future consumers.
